From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@state-edu.gov>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement-counsel@state-edu.gov, Ben Rogers <ben.rogers@stateboard.gov>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Request: DPIA & SCCs for Redwood Inference - State Board procurement

Mina,

Thanks — the procurement committee reviewed Redwood's RFP response and has a few outstanding compliance items we need before we can advance to the vendor selection panel: 

1) Completed DPIA (we've attached the state's DPIA template to this message for vendors).
2) Confirmation that Redwood will accept SCCs (standard contractual clauses) for international transfers OR a copy of your proposed privacy addendum redline.
3) Evidentiary artifacts: latest SOC 2 attestation (redacted OK), completed CAIQ questionnaire or SIG profile, and a list of subprocessors with country and purpose.
4) Clarification on FedRAMP-adjacent requirements: our security team wants a control mapping to NIST 800-53 moderate baseline and confirmation of any cloud-authority/alignment statements. We understand you are hosted; please confirm whether you will sign anything resembling a FedRAMP POA&M commitment or only provide control mappings.

Can you confirm a timeline for: (a) returning a redline of our privacy addendum (we need initial redlines within 5 business days), and (b) delivering DPIA answers and evidence (10 business days preferred)?

Also please indicate the preferred point-of-contact for technical evidence (SOC2/CAIQ) and your procurement counsel contact for contract redlines.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — the committee meets Nov 20.

Best,
Marta Lopez
Senior Procurement Officer
State Board of Education
[Attachment: DPIA_template.docx (docx)]

Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 08:27:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Request: DPIA & SCCs for Redwood Inference - State Board procurement

Mina / Karthik —

Thank you for the quick acknowledgement. A couple clarifications from the committee's side: 

- Data residency: primary requirement is that production-hosted customer data for state tenants remains within US jurisdictions (they listed a few acceptable regions; us-east-1 is preferred). Please confirm reachable options and whether you support customer-managed keys (CMK) or HSM-bound keys for at-rest encryption.
- SOC2: a redacted SOC2 report will be acceptable; we also accept an AICPA letter of attestation.
- FedRAMP-adjacent: the committee understands you are not FedRAMP authorized. They will accept a NIST 800-53 mapping + any existing third-party assessments that align to moderate impact (e.g., a cloud provider's compliance documentation). We will not ask you to represent FedRAMP authorization.

Procurement counsel asked whether Redwood can provide the subprocessors list with contract dates and data classifications for each subprocessors' function. Also — do you have a standard DPA template (if so, please attach), or will you redline ours?

Thanks,
Marta

[Note: State procurement timeline still targets vendor selection week of Nov 22; earlier evidence improves chances of recommendation.]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@state-edu.gov>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: security-ops@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 15:34:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Request: DPIA & SCCs for Redwood Inference - State Board procurement

Hi Marta — attaching the initial evidence pack per your ask. Items attached: SOC2_Attestation_redacted.pdf (we've redacted tenant-specific identifiers), CAIQ_completed.pdf, Subprocessors_list.csv, and a one-page summary of our NIST 800-53 mapping.

Quick notes: 
- Regions: we can provision tenant workloads in us-east-1 and us-west-2; production customer data for state tenants can be restricted to those regions.
- Encryption: we support AES-256 at-rest encryption. We offer customer-managed keys via our KMS integration (customer brings KMS keys or we can use provider-managed keys). For HSM-backed keys we integrate with customer KMS/HSM providers; we do not operate on-prem HSMs for keys.
- Subprocessors: list includes our cloud provider, telemetry/monitoring providers, and a small analytics vendor; CSV includes country and processing purpose. Contracts include standard data processing terms or are covered by our DPA; we can provide effective dates on request.
- FedRAMP-adjacent mapping: we provide a control mapping to NIST 800-53 moderate baseline and a gap summary. We cannot sign a POA&M committing to FedRAMP authorization; instead we supply the mapping and evidence of our control implementations.

Timeline: SOC2 + CAIQ included here; SIG export will follow tomorrow (formatting only). DPIA responses: we can complete the state's DPIA template in ~5 business days if you accept a staged delivery (initial answers then follow-up with technical annexes).

Attachments: SOC2_Attestation_redacted.pdf; CAIQ_completed.pdf; Subprocessors_list.csv; NIST80053_mapping_summary.pdf

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Security & Compliance Engineer
Redwood Inference
